headers.brief: Export, calling-convention and attribute macros of the C ABI.
headers.doc: Self-contained (stdint.h only). ANIRA_API is the export allowlist: hidden visibility everywhere, dllexport/dllimport on Windows, empty inside a static embedding. ANIRA_CALL pins __cdecl on 32-bit Windows. ANIRA_NONBLOCKING marks the real-time entries and callback slots for clang's function-effects analysis and RealtimeSanitizer. ANIRA_INIT spells a compound literal in C and a braced temporary in C++; ANIRA_PTR is the 8-byte pointer slot of every Tier-1 record.

entities.text:
#if defined(__EMSCRIPTEN__)
#define ANIRA_API __attribute__((visibility("default"))) /* plus the generated -sEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS */
#elif defined(ANIRA_STATIC)
#define ANIRA_API /* hidden inside the embedding plugin; PUBLIC on static targets */
#elif defined(_WIN32)
#if defined(ANIRA_BUILDING)
#define ANIRA_API __declspec(dllexport) /* dllexport is the allowlist on PE */
#else
#define ANIRA_API __declspec(dllimport)
#endif
#elif defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)
#define ANIRA_API __attribute__((visibility("default"))) /* plus the version script (SYMBOL anira_*) */
#else
#define ANIRA_API
#endif

#if defined(_WIN32) && !defined(_WIN64)
#define ANIRA_CALL __cdecl /* fixed forever, as CLAP_ABI */
#else
#define ANIRA_CALL
#endif

#if defined(__clang__) && defined(__has_attribute)
#if __has_attribute(nonblocking)
#define ANIRA_NONBLOCKING __attribute__((nonblocking))
#endif
#endif
#ifndef ANIRA_NONBLOCKING
#define ANIRA_NONBLOCKING
#endif

#if defined(__cplusplus)
#define ANIRA_NOEXCEPT noexcept
#define ANIRA_INIT(type, ...) (type{__VA_ARGS__})
#else
#define ANIRA_NOEXCEPT
#define ANIRA_INIT(type, ...) ((type){__VA_ARGS__})
#endif

/* An 8-byte pointer slot on ILP32 and LP64 alike: zero the struct before use, the high
   half of the slot is otherwise undefined on 32-bit targets. */
#define ANIRA_PTR(T, name) \
    union {                \
        T* name;           \
        uint64_t name##_bits; \
    }

#if defined(_MSC_VER) && !defined(__clang__)
#define ANIRA_DEPRECATED(msg) __declspec(deprecated(msg))
#elif defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)
#define ANIRA_DEPRECATED(msg) __attribute__((deprecated(msg)))
#else
#define ANIRA_DEPRECATED(msg)
#endif

headers.brief: Status codes, the anira_error record and the opaque handle types.
headers.doc: Every fallible function returns anira_status; positive values are informational successes and the set a function may return is not frozen, so the stable failure test is ANIRA_FAILED(s), never s != ANIRA_OK. Functions that can produce a message take a nullable anira_error* as their last parameter and fill it on failure, with every out-parameter left untouched.

entities.name: anira_status
entities.doc: Return status of every fallible entry point: 0 is success, positive values are informational successes, negative values are failures.

values.name: ANIRA_SUCCESS_UPGRADED
values.doc: Success; a version 2 JSON document was auto-upgraded (section 8.4).

values.name: ANIRA_INCOMPLETE
values.doc: Success; the enumeration buffer was too short and holds what fit.

values.name: ANIRA_TIMEOUT
values.doc: A wait ran out of time.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
values.doc: A single argument is out of range or NULL where a value is required.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_INVALID_STATE
values.doc: The object is not in a state that allows the call.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED
values.doc: Backend, domain or extension kind not in this build.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_NO_SUCH_FILE
values.doc: A path does not resolve to a readable file.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_ENGINE
values.doc: The engine failed at run time.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_CONFIG
values.doc: Prepare-time legality (section 2), and the real-time refusals recorded in anira_handler_rt_error: a submitted tensor's dtype or axis-tag sequence, a ring or tensor accessor's dtype, a non-F32 Static slot met by the float scalars.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_EXTENSION_UNCONSUMED
values.text: extension not consumed by any stage or adapter
values.doc: An extension was set that nothing in the pipeline consumes (section 1b).

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_EXTENSION_UNKNOWN
values.doc: The extension kind is not registered in this build.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_EDGE_UNREACHABLE
values.text: no edge between the domain and the backend
values.doc: No edge connects the tensor's domain with the selected backend (section 7).

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_BUDGET
values.text: the hard contract's budget cannot be met

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_CAPACITY
values.text: no free slot or ring full
values.doc: Real-time: no free ticket slot, or a ring is full.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_TICKET_STALE
values.doc: The ticket names a recycled slot.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_WRONG_CONTRACT
values.text: wrong contract kind for this entry
values.doc: A Hard entry under an Async contract or vice versa.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_NOT_PREPARED
values.doc: The handler has not been prepared.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_JSON
values.doc: A JSON document is malformed or names an unknown value; the message carries the key path.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_ABI_VERSION
values.doc: anira_check_abi: the header and the library disagree.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL
values.doc: A (buf, cap, out_len) text buffer is too small; out_len holds the required size.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_DEVICE
values.doc: A device descriptor was refused or a device call failed.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_EXTENSION_VERSION
values.doc: The extension kind is known but not at that version.

values.name: ANIRA_ERROR_INTERNAL
values.doc: An exception the firewall could not classify; a bug in anira.

entities.name: ANIRA_FAILED
entities.doc: The only stable failure test: true for every negative status. A minor may add positive (informational) statuses, so never compare against ANIRA_OK.

entities.name: ANIRA_SUCCEEDED
entities.doc: The complement of ANIRA_FAILED.

entities.name: ANIRA_ERROR_MESSAGE_CAPACITY
entities.doc: Capacity of anira_error::message including the terminating NUL.

The opaque handle types. Config handles are value-like (copied at the create that takes them, anira_context_create, anira_handler_create and anira_handler_prepare, destroyable right after); the runtime handles are refcounted internally. Every anira_<x>_destroy is NULL-safe.

entities.name: anira_error
entities.doc: Caller-owned error record, filled by the callee on failure: the status and a NUL-terminated message. Tier 1: 520 bytes, frozen; identical on every target, so anira::Result<T> value-initialises it and TypeScript allocates it with anira_sizeof(ANIRA_STRUCT_ERROR).

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The anira_status of the failure; ANIRA_OK after ANIRA_ERROR_INIT.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: UTF-8, NUL-terminated; empty when no message was produced.

init.name: ANIRA_ERROR_INIT
init.doc: An anira_error with ANIRA_OK and an empty message.

entities.name: anira_status_string
entities.doc: Static text for a status code, for diagnostics; never NULL. An unknown value yields "unknown status".
entities.return_doc: A NUL-terminated string in static storage.

headers.brief: ABI version packing and negotiation, and the library's release identity.
headers.doc: ANIRA_ABI_MAJOR / ANIRA_ABI_MINOR come from the generated build_info.h, derived from the git tag by cmake/build-info.cmake: 0.N through the pre-releases, X.Y from v3.0.0 on. anira_check_abi is the one negotiation call: exact match while the major is 0, same major and a library minor at least the header's afterwards.

entities.name: ANIRA_MAKE_ABI_VERSION
entities.doc: Packs an ABI pair into one uint32_t: major in the high 16 bits, minor in the low 16.

entities.name: ANIRA_ABI_VERSION
entities.doc: The packed ABI version this header was compiled against; what descriptors carry in abi_version and what anira_check_abi takes.

entities.name: ANIRA_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR
entities.doc: The major of a packed ABI version.

entities.name: ANIRA_ABI_VERSION_MINOR
entities.doc: The minor of a packed ABI version.

entities.name: anira_abi_version
entities.doc: The ANIRA_ABI_VERSION the library was built with.
entities.return_doc: The packed pair; unpack with ANIRA_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR / ANIRA_ABI_VERSION_MINOR.

entities.name: anira_check_abi
entities.doc: Negotiates the header the caller compiled against with the library it loaded: ANIRA_OK iff the majors are equal and the library's minor is at least the header's; while the major is 0 (before v3.0.0) the pair must match exactly.
entities.return_doc: ANIRA_OK, or ANIRA_ERROR_ABI_VERSION.

entities.name: anira_version
entities.doc: The library's release version, packed as ANIRA_MAKE_VERSION(major, minor, patch).
entities.return_doc: The packed semver triple of the library.

entities.name: anira_version_string
entities.doc: The library's full version string (git describe without the leading v), e.g. "3.0.0-alpha.1-12-gabc123"; what ANIRA_VERSION_STRING was for the build that produced the library.
entities.return_doc: A NUL-terminated string in static storage.

headers.brief: Every enum and pinned sentinel of the C ABI.
headers.doc: Every value is pinned independently of build options; every enum is a C enum with explicit values and a _FORCE32 = 0x7fffffff terminator, appears as the enum type in parameters and as uint32_t in struct fields, and is exactly four bytes. Engine and execution provider are two independent axes. Reserved ranges are stated per enum.

entities.name: anira_bool
entities.doc: Boolean at the boundary: 0 is false, any other value true.

entities.name: anira_dtype
entities.doc: Packed element type: code | bits << 8 | lanes << 16, whose little-endian bytes are exactly DLPack's DLDataType {uint8 code; uint8 bits; uint16 lanes}.

entities.name: anira_ticket
entities.doc: A job ticket: slot in the low 16 bits, generation in the high 16; a value type, never a heap object.

entities.name: anira_dtype_code
entities.doc: The DLPack type codes carried in the low byte of an anira_dtype.

entities.name: ANIRA_MAKE_DTYPE
entities.ts: (code: number, bits: number, lanes: number): number => (code | (bits << 8) | (lanes << 16)) >>> 0
entities.doc: Packs an anira_dtype from a DLPack code, a bit width and a lane count.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_CODE
entities.doc: The anira_dtype_code of a packed dtype.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_BITS
entities.doc: The bit width of a packed dtype.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_LANES
entities.doc: The lane count of a packed dtype.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_F32
entities.doc: 32-bit float, one lane: the type of every 2.x stream, the ring dtype of every tensor never set on a Hard contract and the only one the float Hard entries carry.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_F64
entities.doc: 64-bit float, one lane.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_F16
entities.doc: 16-bit float.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_BF16
entities.doc: bfloat16.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_I8
entities.doc: Signed 8-bit integer.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_U8
entities.doc: Unsigned 8-bit integer.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_I16
entities.doc: Signed 16-bit integer.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_I32
entities.doc: Signed 32-bit integer.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_I64
entities.doc: Signed 64-bit integer.

entities.name: ANIRA_DTYPE_BOOL8
entities.doc: 8-bit boolean.

entities.name: ANIRA_MAX_RANK
entities.doc: Maximum tensor rank: the axis arrays of anira_tensor and anira_tensor_spec hold this many entries.

entities.name: ANIRA_DYNAMIC
entities.doc: A spec extent that is decided at run time; legal on the Time axis of a Streamed or Buffer spec only.

entities.name: ANIRA_UNBOUNDED
entities.doc: window_max without an upper limit.

entities.name: anira_domain
entities.doc: Where a tensor's bytes live. Values 13..63 are reserved for later domains; every arm named here is pinned now even where no engine reads it before M4.

values.name: ANIRA_DOMAIN_OPAQUE_FD
values.doc: Exported opaque memory (fd, or the NT handle on Windows).

values.name: ANIRA_DOMAIN_WGPU_BUFFER
values.doc: A WGPUBuffer of the context's Dawn device.

values.name: ANIRA_DOMAIN_DMABUF
values.doc: Exported buffer memory as a dma-buf.

values.name: ANIRA_DOMAIN_FRAME
values.doc: Reserved: the Frame side of a FrameToTensor edge (section 1a); nothing consumes it at v3.0.0.

entities.name: anira_sync_kind
entities.doc: The kind of fence an anira_sync_token carries; NONE means the data is already visible.

values.name: ANIRA_SYNC_NONE
values.doc: No fence: the data is visible.

values.name: ANIRA_SYNC_QUEUE_ORDERED
values.doc: Complete when the producing queue reaches it; a same-queue consumer waits for nothing.

values.name: ANIRA_SYNC_VK_TIMELINE
values.doc: A Vulkan timeline semaphore plus value.

values.name: ANIRA_SYNC_SYNC_FILE_FD
values.doc: A sync_file fd (dma-buf / AHardwareBuffer world); owned by the token.

values.name: ANIRA_SYNC_OPAQUE_FD_SEMAPHORE
values.doc: A Vulkan semaphore exported OPAQUE_FD, the only fence CUDA imports; owned by the token.

entities.name: anira_tensor_flags
entities.doc: Bit flags of anira_tensor::flags.

values.name: ANIRA_TENSOR_READ_ONLY
values.doc: The producer will not write; anira must not either.

values.name: ANIRA_TENSOR_DISCARD_CONTENTS
values.doc: The previous contents need not be preserved.

values.name: ANIRA_TENSOR_HOST_COHERENT
values.doc: Host writes are visible without an explicit flush.

entities.name: anira_struct_id
entities.doc: Identifies a record for anira_sizeof (M2): the six Tier-1 PODs and the enumerated Tier-2 records. Ids 0x0001xxxx are reserved for extension payloads, 0x0004xxxx for Emscripten-only structs. The document pins 1..3 and 7..11; 4..6 follow its Tier-1 table order.

entities.name: anira_container
entities.doc: The container of a Frame (section 1a; values reserved at v3.0.0, consumed by abi/draft/frame.h).

entities.name: ANIRA_FOURCC
entities.ts: (a: number, b: number, c: number, d: number): number => (a | (b << 8) | (c << 16) | (d << 24)) >>> 0
entities.doc: A DRM-style fourcc code from four characters.

entities.name: anira_pixel_format
entities.doc: Pixel formats of a Frame; every value is the literal DRM fourcc constant of the format the name abbreviates.

entities.name: anira_color_matrix
entities.doc: YCbCr matrix of a Frame.

entities.name: anira_color_range
entities.doc: Sample range of a Frame.

entities.name: anira_axis_tag
entities.doc: The meaning of one axis of a tensor spec. Axis index order is model memory order (NCHW vs NHWC is just axis order); chunkers find the Time axis by tag.

values.name: ANIRA_AXIS_TIME
values.doc: Time: the axis a Streamed spec is consumed along.

entities.name: anira_role
entities.doc: How a tensor spec is fed and drained.

values.name: ANIRA_ROLE_STREAMED
values.doc: Has a Time axis consumed window-wise (inputs and outputs).

values.name: ANIRA_ROLE_BUFFER
values.doc: The whole submitted buffer is one model tensor, no Time axis (frames, images).

values.name: ANIRA_ROLE_STATIC
values.doc: No time semantics: conditioning in, scalar or embedding out; one value per job.

entities.name: anira_contract_kind
entities.doc: The scheduling regime of a contract.

values.name: ANIRA_CONTRACT_HARD
values.doc: Real-time: the host callback drives fixed or ranged blocks; the v2 regime.

values.name: ANIRA_CONTRACT_ASYNC
values.doc: Asynchronous: jobs with tickets, an optional deadline.

entities.name: anira_budget_kind
entities.doc: How a Hard contract's per-inference budget is set.

values.name: ANIRA_BUDGET_EXPLICIT
values.doc: The explicit_ms of anira_contract_hard_set_budget; the v2 max_inference_time.

entities.name: anira_warmup_mode
entities.doc: Warmup policy of a Hard contract.

values.name: ANIRA_WARMUP_NONE
values.doc: No warmup; legal only with an explicit budget.

values.name: ANIRA_WARMUP_FIXED
values.doc: A fixed number of iterations; the v2 warm_up.

entities.name: anira_miss_policy
entities.doc: What a Hard contract delivers when an inference misses its deadline.

values.name: ANIRA_MISS_BYPASS
values.doc: Pass the input through (default); requires shape-compatible I/O along the anchored Time axis.

entities.name: anira_late_policy
entities.doc: What an Async contract does with a job past its deadline.

values.name: ANIRA_LATE_DROP
values.doc: Cancel at chunk boundaries; enables admission control at dispatch.

entities.name: anira_priority
entities.doc: Scheduling priority of Async jobs.

values.name: ANIRA_PRIORITY_AUTO
values.doc: INTERACTIVE iff a deadline is set, else BATCH (default).

entities.name: anira_delivery
entities.doc: Where an Async completion callback runs.

values.name: ANIRA_DELIVERY_POLLED
values.doc: In the caller of anira_handler_poll / ticket_wait (default).

entities.name: anira_edge_cost
entities.doc: Plan validation policy for the edges a pipeline uses (section 7); not scheduling.

entities.name: ANIRA_WAIT_FOREVER
entities.doc: timeout_ms sentinel of the _wait twins: wait without limit (the v2 set_non_realtime behaviour).

entities.name: ANIRA_WAIT_CONTRACT
entities.doc: timeout_ms sentinel of the _wait twins: wait_ratio times the block duration (the v2 blocking_ratio).

entities.name: anira_ownership
entities.doc: Who owns the device a descriptor names.

values.name: ANIRA_OWNERSHIP_BORROWED
values.doc: The user's handles; anira never destroys them.

values.name: ANIRA_OWNERSHIP_OWNED
values.doc: anira creates and destroys the device.

entities.name: anira_exec_policy
entities.doc: Who pumps a WebGPU device (ProcessEvents / WaitAny).

entities.name: anira_gl_threads
entities.doc: How anira reaches a GL context.

values.name: ANIRA_GL_CALLER_THREAD
values.doc: Only inside allocate_*, submit and bind_output, on the calling thread where the user's context is current (default).

values.name: ANIRA_GL_SHARED_CONTEXT
values.doc: A second context of the same share group that anira's worker makes current (additive).

entities.name: anira_wait_strategy
entities.doc: How idle inference threads wait; the v2 WaitStrategy.

entities.name: anira_log_level
entities.doc: Log severity; the four v2 levels, numerically as the engines count them.

entities.name: anira_log_drain
entities.doc: Who drains the real-time log queue.

values.name: ANIRA_LOG_DRAIN_THREAD
values.doc: anira's low-priority drain thread, every drain_interval_ms (default).

values.name: ANIRA_LOG_DRAIN_MANUAL
values.doc: The host, through anira_drain_log; forced on Wasm.

entities.name: anira_edge_class
entities.doc: Cost class of an edge between a domain and a backend (section 7).

entities.name: anira_probe_rung
entities.doc: The rung a context probe reached for an edge (section 4).

entities.name: ANIRA_THREADS_AUTO
entities.doc: num_threads sentinel: the library's default pool size; 0 means bring your own threads.

entities.name: ANIRA_LOG_FLAG_DISABLE_PLATFORM_SINK
entities.doc: Log flag: switch the platform sink (stderr, logcat, os_log) off while this context lives.

entities.name: ANIRA_LOG_FLAG_TRACE_FAILURES
entities.doc: Log flag: every failed status of every C entry also emits one Error record whose text is the anira_error message prefixed by the entry and the status (the boundary trace, for an application that swallowed the status and a developer who only has the device log). Off by default on every platform. Held while a context that set it lives, counted across contexts.x runtime applies it, in this pre-release the process-wide switch is anira::capi::set_trace_failures.

entities.name: anira_model_state
entities.doc: Whether a model carries state across inferences.

values.name: ANIRA_MODEL_STATEFUL
values.doc: Stateful: session-exclusive, lanes forced to 1; the v2 session_exclusive_processor.

entities.name: anira_bytes_ownership
entities.doc: Whether model bytes handed to a config are copied or borrowed.

values.name: ANIRA_BYTES_BORROW
values.doc: Borrowed until the last carrier dies (the plugin default for embedded blobs); the release callback fires once.

entities.name: ANIRA_AXIS_INSERT
entities.doc: In the axes of anira_model_config_set_tensor_layout: an axis of extent 1 that the entry's file has and the spec does not (a TensorFlow export's rank-3 scalar against a rank-1 spec).

entities.name: anira_ticket_status
entities.doc: The state of an Async job.

entities.name: anira_pad_policy
entities.doc: What happens to a submitted buffer shorter than the window minimum.

entities.name: ANIRA_TICKET_INVALID
entities.doc: The ticket value that names no job; every failed submit writes it.

entities.name: anira_engine
entities.doc: Inference engine, one of the two independent backend axes. Values 6..0x0fff are reserved for later anira engines; a registered custom engine is assigned a value from 0x1000 up at prepare, scoped to its pipeline.

values.name: ANIRA_ENGINE_NONE
values.doc: No engine; as a default engine it means models[0].

entities.name: anira_provider
entities.doc: Execution provider, the other backend axis; a provider name means the same thing across engines.

values.name: ANIRA_PROVIDER_DEFAULT
values.doc: The engine's own CPU path (JSON: no suffix).

entities.name: anira_stage_phase
entities.doc: The phase a stage callback runs in (abi/stage.h, M2); pinned now.

values.name: ANIRA_PHASE_PRE_PROCESS
values.doc: Before the model inputs are formed.

values.name: ANIRA_PHASE_BEFORE_INFERENCE
values.doc: On the inference thread, before the engine call.

values.name: ANIRA_PHASE_AFTER_INFERENCE
values.doc: On the inference thread, after the engine call.

headers.brief: The log sink descriptor, the frozen log record and the logging entry points.
headers.doc: Logging crosses the ABI as anira_log_desc in and anira_log_record out. Real-time paths write fixed-size records into a lock-free queue that a drain thread or the host (anira_drain_log) delivers to the sinks; control paths log synchronously. The sink runs on whichever thread logs, never on the driver thread, possibly with anira's lifecycle lock held, and therefore must not call anira.

entities.name: ANIRA_LOG_RECORD_REALTIME
entities.doc: anira_log_record flag: the record came through the real-time queue.

entities.name: ANIRA_LOG_RECORD_CONTRACT_VIOLATION
entities.doc: anira_log_record flag: the record reports a contract violation raised by the C layer or the wrapper.

entities.name: anira_log_record
entities.doc: One delivered log record, valid for the duration of the callback. Tier 1: 56 bytes, frozen; a projection of the private logger's record.

fields.name: dropped_before
fields.doc: Records the queue dropped before this one.

entities.name: anira_log_fn

params.name: record
params.doc: The record; valid until the callback returns.

entities.doc: A log sink. Runs on whichever thread logs (the caller of a [main-thread] entry, the drain thread for real-time records, the caller of a destroy for the final flush), never on the driver thread; may run with anira's lifecycle lock held and must not call anira.

entities.name: anira_log_desc
entities.doc: The log block of a context config, handed once to anira_context_config_set_log; the C one-shot equivalent of the five scalar setters.

fields.name: callback
fields.doc: The sink; NULL keeps the platform sink only.

fields.name: level
fields.doc: anira_log_level; the most verbose request across contexts wins.

fields.name: queue_capacity
fields.doc: Real-time queue records, clamped to [64, 65536]; fixed for the life of the core.

init.name: ANIRA_LOG_DESC_INIT
init.value: sizeof(anira_log_desc), ANIRA_ABI_VERSION, NULL, NULL, ANIRA_LOG_WARNING, ANIRA_LOG_DRAIN_THREAD, 512, 10, 0, 0
init.doc: The defaults: no sink, WARNING, the drain thread every 10 ms, 512 records.

entities.name: anira_drain_log
entities.doc: Delivers the queued real-time records of this copy's core to the sinks; the host's pump under ANIRA_LOG_DRAIN_MANUAL (and on Wasm, where no drain thread exists). Returns 0 while no core exists. Real-time records are also delivered on the thread of a failing main-thread entry: before a negative status is returned the firewall drains the queue there, so the records that preceded the failure are in front of the host before it acts.
entities.return_doc: The number of records delivered.

entities.name: anira_log_rt

params.name: group
params.doc: "anira.<component>" or the host's own group; static storage.

params.name: static_message
params.doc: A static string, never a format string.

entities.doc: Real-time logging for callers on an ANIRA_NONBLOCKING path: writes "<message> [arg0 arg1]" into the real-time queue without formatting or allocating; a full queue drops and counts. A no-op while no core exists.

entities.name: anira_log
entities.doc: Control-path logging through anira's private logger; formats and allocates like any other control-path call and reaches every sink synchronously.

headers.brief: The configuration handles: tensor specs, model, context, contract and job options, their scalar setters, the device descriptors and the extension slots.
headers.doc: Every entry is [main-thread] and may allocate; a rejected value is ANIRA_FAILED(status), with anira_error::message filled where the entry takes one, and the handle is left as it was. The handle layouts never enter the ABI. Extensions (section 1b) arrive through a set_ext / set_ext_json pair on every handle, one slot per kind, a second set of the same kind replacing the first: a known kind at a registered version is deep-copied during the call, a known kind at an unregistered version is ANIRA_ERROR_EXTENSION_VERSION, an unknown kind is stored and fails prepare by name (ANIRA_ERROR_EXTENSION_UNKNOWN). headers.brief: The context handle over the core, its capabilities and the probe.
headers.doc: anira_context is a refcounted handle over the immortal core, one core per copy of anira (a shared library has one, every static embedding its own). anira_context_create reconciles the context config into the core (the first context's config takes effect whole; later contexts reconcile per field: wait strategy first wins, log level most verbose wins, the thread pool only shrinks and never to zero, drain mode, queue capacity and drain interval first win with a warning), registers the config's log sink and probes the capabilities. The clock and the shutdown family of the core are abi/core.h. Two contexts in one copy are two views of one core with two log sinks. Thread pool and inference queue are core-owned and exist exactly while any handler in this copy exists; anira_shutdown is refused while a context or a handler lives. In this pre-release every context is Host-only: the probe reports the compiled-in engines on ANIRA_PROVIDER_DEFAULT, the host domain and one zero-copy edge per engine; a device block on the config is ANIRA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED at create.

headers.brief: The core of this copy of anira: its steady clock and the shutdown family.
headers.doc: One core per copy of anira (a shared library has one, every static embedding its own) holds what every context and handler shares: the inference thread pool and queue, the backend processor pools, the real-time log queue and its drain. It is created by the first call that needs it and lives until the copy is unloaded; a host never creates or destroys it, it only asks it to shut its threads down (anira_shutdown) or to free itself once nothing uses it (anira_release_core_if_idle), both for a static embedding about to be unloaded. anira_now_ms / anira_now_ns are the steady clock deadlines are spelled in.

entities.name: anira_now_ms
entities.doc: The steady clock in milliseconds, for deadlines and submit timestamps; the same clock as anira_now_ns.
entities.return_doc: Milliseconds since an unspecified steady epoch.

entities.name: anira_now_ns
entities.doc: The steady clock in nanoseconds; the one allowlisted 64-bit return on an ANIRA_NONBLOCKING declaration.
entities.return_doc: Nanoseconds since an unspecified steady epoch.

entities.name: anira_shutdown
entities.doc: Stops and joins the core's inference threads and its log drain thread and flushes the queue, for a static embedding that is about to be unloaded (called from clap_deinit or ExitDll). Idempotent, never creates the core, and effective only when no context and no handler exist in this copy: otherwise nothing happens, so one client of a shared library cannot silence another's sessions.
entities.return_doc: ANIRA_OK (also without a core); ANIRA_ERROR_INVALID_STATE while a context or a handler lives.

entities.name: anira_release_core_if_idle
entities.doc: Frees the core when nothing uses it: no context, no handler, no pool thread, no user-driven inference thread and, on WebAssembly, no inference loop still running. Never blocks; the unload hook's call.
entities.return_doc: Nonzero when the core was freed.

entities.name: anira_has_core
entities.doc: Whether this copy of anira holds a core.
entities.return_doc: Nonzero while the core exists.

headers.brief: User-driven inference threads, the WebAssembly Worker's primitive.
headers.doc: A host that configured its context with num_threads = 0 drives inference itself: it creates anira_inference_thread objects, bound to the core's queue, and either lets anira start an OS thread for each (anira_inference_thread_start, native only) or runs the loop on a thread of its own (anira_inference_thread_run_loop, the only form on WebAssembly, where the thread is a Worker). The objects outlive the context that created them and must be stopped before the library is unloaded.

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_create

params.name: context
params.doc: The context whose core the thread serves; the thread waits with the core's reconciled wait strategy, the first user's.

entities.doc: Creates an inference thread bound to the core's queue. Nothing runs until anira_inference_thread_start or anira_inference_thread_run_loop; on WebAssembly the object is created on the main instance and run in a Worker.
entities.return_doc: ANIRA_OK, or ANIRA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a NULL context or out.

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_run_loop
entities.doc: Runs the inference loop on the calling thread until anira_inference_thread_stop; sets has_exited on return. The caller's thread is an inference thread while it is inside.

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_execute
entities.doc: One step of the loop: dequeues and dispatches one inference if any is pending. The dequeue is allocation-free; the engine call and host callbacks may allocate and block.
entities.return_doc: Nonzero when an inference was dispatched.

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_start
entities.doc: Native: spawns an OS thread at the inference-thread scheduling class (real-time where granted) that runs the loop. WebAssembly: marks the object running; the loop is entered by the Worker through anira_inference_thread_run_loop. A second start while the loop runs, and an operating system that refuses the thread, are returned, never silent: is_running stays 0 then.
entities.return_doc: ANIRA_OK; ANIRA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a NULL thread; ANIRA_ERROR_INVALID_STATE when it is already running; ANIRA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the operating system refused to create the thread (a thread limit or its stack).

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_stop
entities.doc: Requests the loop to exit. Native: joins the OS thread before returning. WebAssembly: requests only; poll anira_inference_thread_has_exited.

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_has_exited
entities.doc: Nonzero once a run of the loop returned (a shared-memory atomic, readable from every WebAssembly instance); required before anira_inference_thread_destroy on WebAssembly.
entities.return_doc: Nonzero after the loop returned; 0 before it ran and while it runs.

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_should_exit
entities.doc: Nonzero once a stop was requested.
entities.return_doc: The stop flag.

entities.name: anira_inference_thread_is_running
entities.doc: Nonzero while the loop is running (native: the OS thread exists and has not returned; WebAssembly: between start and stop).
entities.return_doc: The running flag.

params.doc: The object; NULL is a no-op.

headers.brief: The pipeline, the handler, the plan report and the Hard entries (section 6).
headers.doc: A pipeline is a config object: one inference stage (a model configuration and its candidate backends), copied by anira_handler_create and destroyable right after. A handler is the runtime object over one context: anira_handler_prepare takes a Hard contract, validates the configuration against it, loads the models of the surviving candidates, sizes the rings and builds the plan report; from then on the driver thread pumps samples through the Hard entries, which are ANIRA_NONBLOCKING and never wait, and a thread that may wait calls their _wait twins. Real-time refusals carry no anira_error: the entry returns 0 or a status, records it in anira_handler_rt_error and logs once through the real-time queue. A handler counts as a user of the core: anira_shutdown is refused while one lives. In this pre-release every handler is Host-only, one plan per candidate engine of one variant, an Async contract is refused at prepare, and every ring the handler prepares holds ANIRA_DTYPE_F32 (a ring dtype that differs from its spec's dtype is refused at prepare).

In this pre-release every slot is a host slot: ANIRA_DOMAIN_HOST on both sides, ANIRA_EDGE_ZERO_COPY, recipe "host", no reason.
